summary: Robert F. Rhodes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who pursued doctoral studies at Harvard University. He served as a professor at Otani University, attested between 1993–2000 and 2012–2014.

Robert Florida works in religious and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University and was an Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria (attested 2000–2005).

Robert Ford Campany is a sinologist and religious studies scholar. He was a professor at Indiana University Bloomington (~1989–2004), worked at the University of Southern California (~2004–2010), and joined Vanderbilt University in 2010.

Robert Gardner earned a BA from Harvard University (~1943–1947). He worked at the Fogg Museum and the University of Puget Sound, founded Harvard University in 1957, and was a professor at Harvard from 1956 to 1997.

Robert Gauthiot was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and became a member of the Société Asiatique in 1909.
Robert Göbl was an Iranian, Central Asian, and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of Vienna from 1947 to 1950 and held a post there from circa 1955 to 1989.

Robert H. Brower studied at Harvard (~1940–1944) and Michigan (~1945–1947). In Japanology, he taught at Minnesota (1951–1954), Stanford (1954–1966), and Michigan (1966–1988), also directing the Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies (1963–1964).

Robert H. Sharf studied at Toronto, Kyoto, and Michigan (PhD ~1991 under Luis O. Gómez). A specialist in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, he held posts at McMaster, Kyoto, Michigan, and UC Berkeley.
Robert Hinde studied at St John's College (~1942–1948) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1948–1950). He held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1950 to 1994.

Robert J. Miller was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1956–1988) and as a professor at the American Institute of Indian Studies.
Robert J. Topmiller is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at the University of Kentucky under the supervision of George C. Herring.

Robert Kritzer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley in 1995 under Padmanabh S. Jaini and served as associate professor at Kyoto Notre Dame University (attested 1999–2017).
Robert L. Brown was a scholar of Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a curator at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (~1980–2014) and Professor Emeritus at UCLA (~1986–2014).

Robert Lenz studied at Dorpat/Tartu and under Franz Bopp in Berlin (Dr. Ph. 1831–1832). An Indology and linguistics scholar, he held posts at the Cathedral School of Tallinn, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and Saint Petersburg State University.

Robert M. Gimello earned a PhD from Columbia University (~1968–1976). A specialist in Buddhist studies and Sinology, he held posts at the University of Arizona (~1981–2006) and Harvard University (~2000–2006).

Robert Maclagan was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and the Royal School of Military Engineering, later serving as Principal of IIT Roorkee from 1847 to 1860.

Robert Magliola earned his PhD at Princeton (~1966–1970). In philosophy and religious/Buddhist studies, he held posts at Purdue, Tamkang University, Assumption University, National Taiwan University (~1985–1998), and Columbia University (2002–2011).

Robert Mayer studied at the University of Bristol (dissertation 1985) and Leiden University (PhD). A specialist in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he became an Oriental Studies faculty member at the University of Oxford in 2002.

Robert Needham Cust studied at Eton, Trinity College Cambridge, East India Company College, Haileybury, and Fort William College. A scholar of linguistics and Indology, he served in the Bengal Civil Service from circa 1843 to 1867.

Robert P. Goldman studied at Columbia and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD ~1971 under Ludo Rocher). An Indologist, he became a professor at the University of California, Berkeley in circa 1971, later serving as professor emeritus.
